messages.subject: Titanium bar non-conformity — Ferncliffe Alloys
messages.plaintextBody:
Sarah,

We have a problem I'd like Whitfield Carter to take on. Ferncliffe Alloys supplied us Ti-6Al-4V bar (heats FA-7733 and FA-7741) under our 2023 supply agreement for the CM-7 wing-rib fittings. It's come back non-conforming on chemistry and we've found alpha-case well outside our spec. We've already scrapped 312 finished fittings and stopped the Bay 4 cell.

Grace will pull the cost numbers together. Can you and the team advise on recovery against Ferncliffe? Helen Forsythe (Ops) and Idris Cole (procurement) will be your day-to-day contacts.

Robert

Robert Falconer
Chief Executive Officer | Halstead Aerospace Limited

messages.subject: RE: Titanium bar non-conformity — Ferncliffe Alloys
messages.plaintextBody:
Robert,

Thank you — yes, we can act. This looks like a straightforward breach-of-warranty/Sale of Goods claim, but causation (was the alpha-case there on delivery or introduced in your process?) will be the battleground, so the metallurgy evidence will be everything. Please preserve all the bar, the retained coupons and the certificates, and don't let anyone scrap or reprocess the remaining stock.

James Osei will lead day to day. First steps: (1) get the independent lab report finalised; (2) lock down the incoming-inspection and storage records; (3) build the loss schedule. We'll send a short engagement note today.

Sarah

Sarah Whitfield
Partner | Whitfield Carter LLP

T +44 (0)20 7946 0012
Confidential and may be legally privileged.

Picking this up. Could you send me, when you have a moment: the supply agreement and our spec HAS-MAT-114, PO HAL-PO-44119, the Ferncliffe certs of conformity and mill certs, the incoming inspection report and NCR QN-2024-0337, and the scrap disposition record. No rush today, but the sooner we have the document trail the sooner we can pin causation.

James
